The final challenge at the Pokemon League is against the Elite Four, a supergroup quartet of powerful trainers who use the game's most powerful types. Though each one has a "main" type, it's more accurate to say they specialize in two types, mostly ones that cover the bases of another. You'll need an incredible team to beat them; anything less than that (bar using an absurd amount of items) will only give you trouble. I recommend having a team at the high end of being Level 40s or early 50s when going in. You can't stop to heal at the Pokemon Center or buy more items at the Poke Mart so be fully prepared going in.   
 The single best Pokemon for this challenge is none other than Lapras. It will wall Lorelei's team and strike back with Thunderbolt, decimate Bruno with a mixture of Psychic and Surf, rip through Agatha's team with Psychic, and completely destroy Lance with Ice Beam. I highly endorse Lapras. Another great Pokemon is Gengar, who can use a variation on this set with Thunderbolt and Psychic and two other strong Special moves (or support). It has the added bonus of being invincible against all Normal-type and Fighting-type moves in the tournament.

Elite Member #1 - Lorelei
**Elite Four**: Lorelei **Specialty**: Water & Ice-type **Details**: The first member of the Elite Four, Lorelei, has an excellent team to start off against. Although she says freezing moves are powerful, only two of her Pokemon can freeze you. Don't think you're off the hook though; when frozen in Generation I, you will never defrost unless hit by a Fire-type move, and unfortunately for you none of her Pokemon carry one. Her leading Pokemon, Dewgong, will use Rest to heal off all damage, so try and take it out quickly or during the turns it's asleep. The move Thunderbolt is excellent for that, and even moreso on a Lapras who can essentially wall her entire team. Slowbro needs to be dispatched extremely quickly as well as Amnesia is frightening: it boosts the Special stat by two. Cloyster has ludicrous Defense and will trap you with Clamp the way Blaine did with Fire Spin. Jynx isn't as bad as the rest of the team if you use strong Rock-type moves, but watch out for a mean Ice Punch from her should you break out a Golem or Onix. Her Lapras is also a terrifying with its Confuse Ray and Blizzard combo - your own Lapras would be the best counter. ![Image 4](https://serebii.net/pokearth/trainers/rby/13.png)[![Image Elite Member #2 - Bruno
**Elite Four**: Bruno **Specialty**: Rock & Fighting-type **Details**: Undeniably the easiest trainer in this challenge, Bruno is still a force to be reckoned with. His team is very akin to Brock and the Fighting Dojo master's teams, using Onix as well as the Hitmons as main staples. His Onix share the exact same movepool; if you finish one off you'll have no problem with the other. Hitmonchan's moveset is practically useless save for Counter, which can totally destroy you if you're taking the route of powerful Flying-type moves on the Fighting-types. Hitmonlee has Jump Kick and Hi Jump Kick, both extremely powerful attacks. A recommended strategy is to use Fly on it with something; if it tries to Jump Kick or Hi Jump Kick you in the turn you're in the air, it will miss and take bad damage from it, setting up for a guaranteed KO the next turn with Fly. Machamp is the only true threat here as it has a great moveset which includes the OHKO move Giovanni gave you. If you have something impervious to ground you'll have no troubles though. A Gengar works wonders here as it avoids all Fighting/Flying moves and strikes back with a buffed-up Psychic. ![Image 21](https://serebii.net/pokearth/trainers/rby/14.png)[![Image Elite Member #3 - Agatha
**Elite Four**: Agatha **Specialty**: Poison & Ghost-type **Details**: This old bird makes great use of the Gastly lines, stuffing her team with two Gengars and a Haunter. This generation has an issue with the type match ups - because of that, Psychics are impervious to Ghost-type moves. A good Pokemon here would be Alakazam, who can sweep the entire team with just Psychic and will have the speed to beat out Gengar and Golbat. As long as you don't get hit by physical attacks you'll be golden. This team loves status moves, with everything being able to do almost anything under the sun, including poison, sleep, confusion, and paralysis. Don't afford them any of those luxuries - confusion will ruin a physical sweeper if it hits itself, sleep will leave you susceptible to Dream Eater (which most of the team save for the non-Ghosts runs), paralysis will lower your much needed Speed, and poison is, well, poison. Ground-type moves are great here too because the Gastly line doesn't have Levitate in this generation, leaving four fifths of the team open to a strong Earthquake or Dig. Don't bother with Normal or Fighting-type moves here though because they'll be useless on the Ghosts. If you are put asleep at any point, remember you can save healing items by using the Poke Flute to awaken. ![Image 35](https://serebii.net/pokearth/trainers/rby/15.png)[![Image Elite Member #4 - Lance
**Elite Four**: Lance **Specialty**: Dragon-type **Details**: The king of the Elite Four, Lance, has the most frightening team of all. Gyarados, his lead, has decent Special in this generation and can wipe you out with Hydro Pump or Hyper Beam depending on what works better. Hyper Beam, by the way, is a staple of his team, and has an interesting quirk - if it knocks a Pokemon out it won't need to recharge. Luckily Gyarados has a double weakness to Electric-type moves, so hit it with those for maximum punishment. His two Dragonairs share a moveset that includes Dragon Rage (a set 40 damage move), Agility, Slam, and Hyper Beam. Dispose of them quickly or use a Rock-type with great Defense to sponge their moves and whittle them down. Rhydon or Golem works wonders here, as does an Omastar with Ice Beam. Aerodactyl is fast and has great Attack but poor moves - in fact, a Gengar can wall it completely. The main attraction, Dragonite, can set up a Barrier to boost Defense then take you out with a Hyper Beam backed by one of the highest Attack stats in the game. It does have a double Ice weakness though - exploit it. ![Image 51](https://serebii.net/pokearth/trainers/rby/16.png)[![Image Champion - Blue
**Elite Four**: Rival **Specialty**: None **Details**: The circle is now complete. Your first and last challenge is with your rival, and he'll have just as many tricks as ever to face you. With a fully rounded out team you'll be hard pressed to find one Pokemon to take everything out; however, if you don't mind legendaries, I recommend Zapdos for its Electric-type (good for beating literally up to 2/3 of the team depending on who he chose, or at the very least half) and Flying-type (provides STAB and good speed to take out Alakazam with a quick physical move). If not, balance everything out as always: don't train just one Pokemon (seriously don't) and make sure your type coverage is astute. His team has a few flaws you can exploit: Arcanine, if he has it, laughably knows Ember as its Fire-type attack, Gyarados's Hyper Beam makes it stall a turn if it doesn't wipe you out, Exeggutor only has three attacks (both damage-inflicting ones of the Normal-type), and Rhydon has a low-accuracy OHKO move it'll try on you. An alternate approach to this is to just use Toxic on everything (use PP Up if you're doing this) and stall it out with Chansey or another bulky Pokemon. It's not exactly enthralling but if it's what works go for it. The final challenge at the Pokemon League is against the Elite Four, a supergroup quartet of powerful trainers who use the game's most powerful types. Though each one has a "main" type, it's more accurate to say they specialize in two types, mostly ones that cover the bases of another. You'll need an incredible team to beat them; anything less than that (bar using an absurd amount of items) will only give you trouble. I recommend having a team at the high end of being Level 40s or early 50s when going in. You can't stop to heal at the Pokemon Center or buy more items at the Poke Mart so be fully prepared going in.   
 The single best Pokemon for this challenge is none other than Lapras. It will wall Lorelei's team and strike back with Thunderbolt, decimate Bruno with a mixture of Psychic and Surf, rip through Agatha's team with Psychic, and completely destroy Lance with Ice Beam. I highly endorse Lapras. Another great Pokemon is Gengar, who can use a variation on this set with Thunderbolt and Psychic and two other strong Special moves (or support). It has the added bonus of being invincible against all Normal-type and Fighting-type moves in the tournament.

Elite Member #1 - Lorelei
**Elite Four**: Lorelei **Specialty**: Water & Ice-type **Details**: The first member of the Elite Four, Lorelei, has an excellent team to start off against. Although she says freezing moves are powerful, only two of her Pokemon can freeze you. Don't think you're off the hook though; when frozen in Generation I, you will never defrost unless hit by a Fire-type move, and unfortunately for you none of her Pokemon carry one. Her leading Pokemon, Dewgong, will use Rest to heal off all damage, so try and take it out quickly or during the turns it's asleep. The move Thunderbolt is excellent for that, and even moreso on a Lapras who can essentially wall her entire team. Slowbro needs to be dispatched extremely quickly as well as Amnesia is frightening: it boosts the Special stat by two. Cloyster has ludicrous Defense and will trap you with Clamp the way Blaine did with Fire Spin. Jynx isn't as bad as the rest of the team if you use strong Rock-type moves, but watch out for a mean Ice Punch from her should you break out a Golem or Onix. Her Lapras is also a terrifying with its Confuse Ray and Blizzard combo - your own Lapras would be the best counter. ![Image 4](https://serebii.net/pokearth/trainers/rby/13.png)[![Image Elite Member #2 - Bruno
**Elite Four**: Bruno **Specialty**: Rock & Fighting-type **Details**: Undeniably the easiest trainer in this challenge, Bruno is still a force to be reckoned with. His team is very akin to Brock and the Fighting Dojo master's teams, using Onix as well as the Hitmons as main staples. His Onix share the exact same movepool; if you finish one off you'll have no problem with the other. Hitmonchan's moveset is practically useless save for Counter, which can totally destroy you if you're taking the route of powerful Flying-type moves on the Fighting-types. Hitmonlee has Jump Kick and Hi Jump Kick, both extremely powerful attacks. A recommended strategy is to use Fly on it with something; if it tries to Jump Kick or Hi Jump Kick you in the turn you're in the air, it will miss and take bad damage from it, setting up for a guaranteed KO the next turn with Fly. Machamp is the only true threat here as it has a great moveset which includes the OHKO move Giovanni gave you. If you have something impervious to ground you'll have no troubles though. A Gengar works wonders here as it avoids all Fighting/Flying moves and strikes back with a buffed-up Psychic. ![Image 21](https://serebii.net/pokearth/trainers/rby/14.png)[![Image Elite Member #3 - Agatha
**Elite Four**: Agatha **Specialty**: Poison & Ghost-type **Details**: This old bird makes great use of the Gastly lines, stuffing her team with two Gengars and a Haunter. This generation has an issue with the type match ups - because of that, Psychics are impervious to Ghost-type moves. A good Pokemon here would be Alakazam, who can sweep the entire team with just Psychic and will have the speed to beat out Gengar and Golbat. As long as you don't get hit by physical attacks you'll be golden. This team loves status moves, with everything being able to do almost anything under the sun, including poison, sleep, confusion, and paralysis. Don't afford them any of those luxuries - confusion will ruin a physical sweeper if it hits itself, sleep will leave you susceptible to Dream Eater (which most of the team save for the non-Ghosts runs), paralysis will lower your much needed Speed, and poison is, well, poison. Ground-type moves are great here too because the Gastly line doesn't have Levitate in this generation, leaving four fifths of the team open to a strong Earthquake or Dig. Don't bother with Normal or Fighting-type moves here though because they'll be useless on the Ghosts. If you are put asleep at any point, remember you can save healing items by using the Poke Flute to awaken. ![Image 35](https://serebii.net/pokearth/trainers/rby/15.png)[![Image Elite Member #4 - Lance
**Elite Four**: Lance **Specialty**: Dragon-type **Details**: The king of the Elite Four, Lance, has the most frightening team of all. Gyarados, his lead, has decent Special in this generation and can wipe you out with Hydro Pump or Hyper Beam depending on what works better. Hyper Beam, by the way, is a staple of his team, and has an interesting quirk - if it knocks a Pokemon out it won't need to recharge. Luckily Gyarados has a double weakness to Electric-type moves, so hit it with those for maximum punishment. His two Dragonairs share a moveset that includes Dragon Rage (a set 40 damage move), Agility, Slam, and Hyper Beam. Dispose of them quickly or use a Rock-type with great Defense to sponge their moves and whittle them down. Rhydon or Golem works wonders here, as does an Omastar with Ice Beam. Aerodactyl is fast and has great Attack but poor moves - in fact, a Gengar can wall it completely. The main attraction, Dragonite, can set up a Barrier to boost Defense then take you out with a Hyper Beam backed by one of the highest Attack stats in the game. It does have a double Ice weakness though - exploit it. ![Image 51](https://serebii.net/pokearth/trainers/rby/16.png)[![Image Champion - Blue
**Elite Four**: Rival **Specialty**: None **Details**: The circle is now complete. Your first and last challenge is with your rival, and he'll have just as many tricks as ever to face you. With a fully rounded out team you'll be hard pressed to find one Pokemon to take everything out; however, if you don't mind legendaries, I recommend Zapdos for its Electric-type (good for beating literally up to 2/3 of the team depending on who he chose, or at the very least half) and Flying-type (provides STAB and good speed to take out Alakazam with a quick physical move). If not, balance everything out as always: don't train just one Pokemon (seriously don't) and make sure your type coverage is astute. His team has a few flaws you can exploit: Arcanine, if he has it, laughably knows Ember as its Fire-type attack, Gyarados's Hyper Beam makes it stall a turn if it doesn't wipe you out, Exeggutor only has three attacks (both damage-inflicting ones of the Normal-type), and Rhydon has a low-accuracy OHKO move it'll try on you. An alternate approach to this is to just use Toxic on everything (use PP Up if you're doing this) and stall it out with Chansey or another bulky Pokemon. It's not exactly enthralling but if it's what works go for it. # Red/Blue Gym Leaders & Elite Four

The standard Pokémon format as initialised here in Red/Blue is to battle your way through 8 gyms, each specializing in a particular type. Following that you take on the Elite Four and the Champion.

### Gym Leaders

1.   Brock(Pewter City)
2.   Misty(Cerulean City)
3.   Lt. Surge(Vermilion City)
4.   Erika(Celadon City)
5.   Koga(Fuchsia City)
6.   Sabrina(Saffron City)
7.   Blaine(Cinnabar Island)
8.   Giovanni(Viridian City)

### Elite Four

1.   Lorelei
2.   Bruno
3.   Agatha
4.   Lance
5.   Blue

With the exception of _[Sword & Shield](https://www.thegamer.com/tag/pokemon-sword-and-shield/),_ each generation of _[Pokémon](https://www.thegamer.com/tag/pokemon/)_ has included an official Elite Four whom the player must defeat before challenging the Champion of the region. Like Gym Leaders, each of the twenty-eight Elite Four members specializes in certain types and come prepared with some of the strongest Pokémon in the Pokédex.

RELATED: [Pokémon: The 10 Toughest Gyms In The Series, Ranked](https://www.thegamer.com/pokemon-toughest-gyms-series-ranked/)

While the Elite Four members are known to be the strongest trainers of their respective region, it can be difficult albeit interesting to gauge how they'd compare against one another. Whether they have a powerful team or clever battle strategies, the best of the best can be ranked accordingly.

## 28  Hala

![Image 6: Hala Drinking Coffee at Home](https://static0.thegamerimages.com/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2020/07/Pokemon-Elite-Four-Hala.jpg?q=50&fit=crop&w=825&dpr=1.5)

Hala is the Fighting-type specialist of the Alola Region's Elite Four. With a lack of variation in his team, all of his Pokémon share the common weaknesses of Flying, Fairy, and Psychic-type attacks.

## 27  Kahili

![Image 7](https://static0.thegamerimages.com/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2020/07/Pokemon-Elite-Four-Kahili.jpg?q=50&fit=crop&w=825&dpr=1.5)

Kahili is the only Elite Four member who specializes in [Flying-type](https://www.thegamer.com/pokemon-which-flying-type-are-you-based-on-your-chinese-zodiac/) Pokémon. Her team composition, however, does not include the best Flying-types out there. Each of her party members can be shot down with a quick Electric attack.

## 26  Koga

![Image 8](https://static0.thegamerimages.com/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2020/07/Pokemon-Elite-Four-Koga.jpg?q=50&fit=crop&w=825&dpr=1.5)

After moving on from being a Kanto Gym Leader, Koga joins the Johto Region's Elite Four. There, he uses a team of [Poison-types](https://www.thegamer.com/pokemon-strongest-poison-type-every-generation/) who lack in sheer offensive and instead rely more on poisoning and stalling out the opponent.

## 25  Olivia

![Image 9: Pokemon Anime Olivia in the anime](https://static0.thegamerimages.com/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2020/07/Pokemon-Elite-Four-Olivia.jpg?q=50&fit=crop&w=825&dpr=1.5)

Olivia is the sole Rock-type specialist amongst the Elite Four members. Her team varies slightly between games _,_ but her Lycanroc remains as her signature Pokémon with the handy Rockium Z.

## 24  Acerola

![Image 10: Acerola smiling in a library](https://static0.thegamerimages.com/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2020/07/Pokemon-Elite-Four-Acerola.jpg?q=50&fit=crop&w=825&dpr=1.5)

Ghost-type specialists are common in the Elite Four, but Acerola is perhaps the most underwhelming amongst her fellow ghost lovers. Any Dark-type Pokémon should be able to tear through her team with relative ease.

## 23  Siebold

![Image 11](https://static0.thegamerimages.com/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2020/07/Pokemon-Elite-Four-Siebold.jpg?q=50&fit=crop&w=825&dpr=1.5)

Despite the fact that Water is the most common type in the game, Siebold is the only Elite Four member who specializes in [Water Pokémon](https://www.thegamer.com/pokemon-ugliest-cutest-water-types/). His team may have a glaring weakness to Grass and Electric attacks, but his four Pokémon have the means to fight back with.

## 22  Lorelei

![Image 12](https://static0.thegamerimages.com/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2020/07/Pokemon-Elite-Four-Lorelei.jpg?q=50&fit=crop&w=825&dpr=1.5)

Siebold might be the only official Water-type specialist, but Gen I's Lorelei has plenty of dual Water-types that go hand in hand with her Ice-type specialty. With Dewgong, Cloyster, and Lapras as her Ice/Water-types, Lorelei can easily counter Fire-types.

## 21  Will

![Image 13](https://static0.thegamerimages.com/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2020/07/Pokemon-Elite-Four-Will.jpg?q=50&fit=crop&w=825&dpr=1.5)

Psychic-type Pokémon are known for their high Special Attack and Special Defense, and that's exactly what Will's team is built around. His Bronzong and Grumpig have good special bulk, while the rest of his team focuses more on offensive special damage.

## 20  Karen

![Image 14: Karen as she appears in Pokemon Masters EX](https://static0.thegamerimages.com/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2020/07/Pokemon-Elite-Four-Karen.jpg?q=50&fit=crop&w=825&dpr=1.5)

Prior to the introduction of Fairy-types, Dark-type Pokémon only had two weaknesses in Bug and Fighting.

RELATED: [Pokémon: Every Gym Leader In The Galar Region, Ranked](https://www.thegamer.com/pokemon-gym-leader-galar-ranked/)

As an Elite Four member of the Johto Region, Karen's Dark team never has to worry about Fairy-types. Instead, she has perfect counters to Bug and Fighting-types.

## 19  Bruno

![Image 15](https://static0.thegamerimages.com/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2020/07/Pokemon-Elite-Four-Bruno.jpg?q=50&fit=crop&w=825&dpr=1.5)

Bruno is the designated [Fighting-type](https://www.thegamer.com/pokemon-best-competitive-fighting-type-ranked/) specialist of the first two generations. His Machamp and Lucario are two of the best when it comes to Fighting-types.

With the exception of _[Sword & Shield](https://www.thegamer.com/tag/pokemon-sword-and-shield/),_ each generation of _[Pokémon](https://www.thegamer.com/tag/pokemon/)_ has included an official Elite Four whom the player must defeat before challenging the Champion of the region. Like Gym Leaders, each of the twenty-eight Elite Four members specializes in certain types and come prepared with some of the strongest Pokémon in the Pokédex.

RELATED: [Pokémon: The 10 Toughest Gyms In The Series, Ranked](https://www.thegamer.com/pokemon-toughest-gyms-series-ranked/)

While the Elite Four members are known to be the strongest trainers of their respective region, it can be difficult albeit interesting to gauge how they'd compare against one another. Whether they have a powerful team or clever battle strategies, the best of the best can be ranked accordingly.

## 28  Hala

![Image 6: Hala Drinking Coffee at Home](https://static0.thegamerimages.com/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2020/07/Pokemon-Elite-Four-Hala.jpg?q=50&fit=crop&w=825&dpr=1.5)

Hala is the Fighting-type specialist of the Alola Region's Elite Four. With a lack of variation in his team, all of his Pokémon share the common weaknesses of Flying, Fairy, and Psychic-type attacks.

## 27  Kahili

![Image 7](https://static0.thegamerimages.com/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2020/07/Pokemon-Elite-Four-Kahili.jpg?q=50&fit=crop&w=825&dpr=1.5)

Kahili is the only Elite Four member who specializes in [Flying-type](https://www.thegamer.com/pokemon-which-flying-type-are-you-based-on-your-chinese-zodiac/) Pokémon. Her team composition, however, does not include the best Flying-types out there. Each of her party members can be shot down with a quick Electric attack.

## 26  Koga

![Image 8](https://static0.thegamerimages.com/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2020/07/Pokemon-Elite-Four-Koga.jpg?q=50&fit=crop&w=825&dpr=1.5)

After moving on from being a Kanto Gym Leader, Koga joins the Johto Region's Elite Four. There, he uses a team of [Poison-types](https://www.thegamer.com/pokemon-strongest-poison-type-every-generation/) who lack in sheer offensive and instead rely more on poisoning and stalling out the opponent.

## 25  Olivia

![Image 9: Pokemon Anime Olivia in the anime](https://static0.thegamerimages.com/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2020/07/Pokemon-Elite-Four-Olivia.jpg?q=50&fit=crop&w=825&dpr=1.5)

Olivia is the sole Rock-type specialist amongst the Elite Four members. Her team varies slightly between games _,_ but her Lycanroc remains as her signature Pokémon with the handy Rockium Z.

## 24  Acerola

![Image 10: Acerola smiling in a library](https://static0.thegamerimages.com/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2020/07/Pokemon-Elite-Four-Acerola.jpg?q=50&fit=crop&w=825&dpr=1.5)

Ghost-type specialists are common in the Elite Four, but Acerola is perhaps the most underwhelming amongst her fellow ghost lovers. Any Dark-type Pokémon should be able to tear through her team with relative ease.

## 23  Siebold

![Image 11](https://static0.thegamerimages.com/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2020/07/Pokemon-Elite-Four-Siebold.jpg?q=50&fit=crop&w=825&dpr=1.5)

Despite the fact that Water is the most common type in the game, Siebold is the only Elite Four member who specializes in [Water Pokémon](https://www.thegamer.com/pokemon-ugliest-cutest-water-types/). His team may have a glaring weakness to Grass and Electric attacks, but his four Pokémon have the means to fight back with.

## 22  Lorelei

![Image 12](https://static0.thegamerimages.com/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2020/07/Pokemon-Elite-Four-Lorelei.jpg?q=50&fit=crop&w=825&dpr=1.5)

Siebold might be the only official Water-type specialist, but Gen I's Lorelei has plenty of dual Water-types that go hand in hand with her Ice-type specialty. With Dewgong, Cloyster, and Lapras as her Ice/Water-types, Lorelei can easily counter Fire-types.

## 21  Will

![Image 13](https://static0.thegamerimages.com/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2020/07/Pokemon-Elite-Four-Will.jpg?q=50&fit=crop&w=825&dpr=1.5)

Psychic-type Pokémon are known for their high Special Attack and Special Defense, and that's exactly what Will's team is built around. His Bronzong and Grumpig have good special bulk, while the rest of his team focuses more on offensive special damage.

## 20  Karen

![Image 14: Karen as she appears in Pokemon Masters EX](https://static0.thegamerimages.com/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2020/07/Pokemon-Elite-Four-Karen.jpg?q=50&fit=crop&w=825&dpr=1.5)

Prior to the introduction of Fairy-types, Dark-type Pokémon only had two weaknesses in Bug and Fighting.

RELATED: [Pokémon: Every Gym Leader In The Galar Region, Ranked](https://www.thegamer.com/pokemon-gym-leader-galar-ranked/)

As an Elite Four member of the Johto Region, Karen's Dark team never has to worry about Fairy-types. Instead, she has perfect counters to Bug and Fighting-types.

## 19  Bruno

![Image 15](https://static0.thegamerimages.com/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2020/07/Pokemon-Elite-Four-Bruno.jpg?q=50&fit=crop&w=825&dpr=1.5)

Bruno is the designated [Fighting-type](https://www.thegamer.com/pokemon-best-competitive-fighting-type-ranked/) specialist of the first two generations. His Machamp and Lucario are two of the best when it comes to Fighting-types.

**Elite Four**

High atop the Indigo Plateau, the Elite Four of Kanto await the challenge of any trainer bold enough to collect all eight badges. This league boasts a knockout style where you battle the trainers back to back, with only a break in between to walk to the next room - so while you can use healing items in between battles, you cannot go back to the Pokemon Center. Proceed with caution.

Elite Four Lorelei
**Member**: Lorelei **Specialty**: Ice-type **Method**: Lorelei uses a mixture of Ice-type and Water-type Pokemon. Her strategy uses a mixture of powerful attacks and applying residual damage in the form of Hail and Spikes. Hail lasts five turns and will hit all non-Ice-types. **Elite Four**

High atop the Indigo Plateau, the Elite Four of Kanto await the challenge of any trainer bold enough to collect all eight badges. This league boasts a knockout style where you battle the trainers back to back, with only a break in between to walk to the next room - so while you can use healing items in between battles, you cannot go back to the Pokemon Center. Proceed with caution.

Elite Four Lorelei
**Member**: Lorelei **Specialty**: Ice-type **Method**: Lorelei uses a mixture of Ice-type and Water-type Pokemon. Her strategy uses a mixture of powerful attacks and applying residual damage in the form of Hail and Spikes. Hail lasts five turns and will hit all non-Ice-types. Rock-type moves are ideal here since the obvious choice of Fire will only hurt Jynx for super-effective damage. ![Image 4](https://www.serebii.net/pokearth/trainers/frlg/18.png)[![Image **Rematches**

After you finish your affairs in the Sevii Islands, you can return to the Indigo Plateau for a second round at the Elite Four. While you've been away these trainers have sharpened their skills, levelling up their teams and throwing in some Johto Pokemon to patch up holes they may have had the first time.

**Member**: Lorelei **Specialty**: Ice-type **Method**: This time around Lorelei has shifted focus and built her team solely around Ice-types, trading the Slowbro for a Piloswine who uses very strong physical moves like Earthquake. [File:LGPE Elite Four (LGPE).png](https://lmts-personal.fandom.com/wiki/Special:Upload?wpDestFile=LGPE_Elite_Four_(LGPE).png "File:LGPE Elite Four (LGPE).png")

Artwork of Chase and Elaine confronting the Kanto Elite Four in [Pokémon: Let's Go, Pikachu! and Let's Go, Eevee!](https://lmts-personal.fandom.com/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon:_Let%27s_Go,_Pikachu!_and_Let%27s_Go,_Eevee! "Pokémon: Let's Go, Pikachu! and Let's Go, Eevee!")

The **Elite Four** (Japanese: **四天王**_The Big Four_) are four [Pokémon Trainers](https://lmts-personal.fandom.com/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Trainer "Pokémon Trainer") who are regarded as the toughest in their [regional](https://lmts-personal.fandom.com/wiki/Region "Region")[Pokémon League](https://lmts-personal.fandom.com/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_League "Pokémon League"), just short of the [Pokémon League Champion](https://lmts-personal.fandom.com/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Champion "Pokémon Champion"). Those who challenge the Elite Four must have won all eight [Badges](https://lmts-personal.fandom.com/wiki/Badge "Badge") from that region (or, for Trainers in [Alola](https://lmts-personal.fandom.com/wiki/Alola "Alola"), must have completed all of their island challenge trials). To become Champion, Trainers must face all four and the current Champion consecutively without losing to any of them. Challengers who lose at any time must start their challenge from the beginning. In Paldea, the challenge is named the Elite Test, and is part of the greater Champion Assessment.

One group resides at the Indigo Plateau in [Kanto](https://lmts-personal.fandom.com/wiki/Kanto "Kanto") and are considered the best Trainers in both Kanto and [Johto](https://lmts-personal.fandom.com/wiki/Johto "Johto"). Another group is located in Ever Grande City in [Hoenn](https://lmts-personal.fandom.com/wiki/Hoenn "Hoenn"), while another is located on Mount Lanakila in [Alola](https://lmts-personal.fandom.com/wiki/Alola "Alola"). Four more groups reside at the Pokémon Leagues in Sinnoh, Unova, Kalos, and Template:Pal.

In the games, they use strong medicine items in battles. In [Generation II](https://lmts-personal.fandom.com/wiki/Generation_II "Generation II"), they use Max Potions, and from [Generation III](https://lmts-personal.fandom.com/wiki/Generation_III "Generation III") onwards, they use Full Restores. Like [Gym Leaders](https://lmts-personal.fandom.com/wiki/Gym_Leader "Gym Leader"), they typically specialize in Pokémon of a particular [type](https://lmts-personal.fandom.com/wiki/Type "Type"). Prior to [Generation V](https://lmts-personal.fandom.com/wiki/Generation_V "Generation V") and in Generation IX, the Elite Four typically progresses in level with their Pokémon in the games and must be challenged in a set order. From Generation V to Generation VII, all members of the Elite Four (except in remakes) use Pokémon of the same levels, as they can be challenged in any order.

In [Generation VIII](https://lmts-personal.fandom.com/wiki/Generation_VIII "Generation VIII"), the Pokémon League in the Galar region uses the Champion Cup tournament instead of an Elite Four.

[File:Sinnoh Elite Four.png](https://lmts-personal.fandom.com/wiki/Special:Upload?wpDestFile=Sinnoh_Elite_Four.png "File:Sinnoh Elite Four.png")

The Sinnoh Elite Four in the anime

In the [Pokémon anime](https://lmts-personal.fandom.com/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_anime "Pokémon anime"), [Ash](https://lmts-personal.fandom.com/wiki/Ash_Ketchum "Ash Ketchum") and [his friends](https://lmts-personal.fandom.com/wiki/Ash%27s_friends "Ash's friends") infrequently meet Elite Four members, who then impart them with battle strategies. In _An Elite Meet and Greet!_, Lucian revealed that when a Trainer wins their respective region's [League Conference](https://lmts-personal.fandom.com/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_League_Conference "Pokémon League Conference"), they can participate in the [Champion League](https://lmts-personal.fandom.com/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_League#Champion_League "Pokémon League"), fighting the members of that region's Elite Four, and, if victorious against them, the regional [Champion](https://lmts-personal.fandom.com/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Champion "Pokémon Champion") as well. It has also been shown that an Elite Four member can challenge the Champion for their title.

#### Kanto Elite Four[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Flmts-personal.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FElite_Four%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D16&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")]

In [Kanto](https://lmts-personal.fandom.com/wiki/Kanto "Kanto"), Ash has met the entire original Elite Four roster:

*   [Bruno](https://lmts-personal.fandom.com/wiki/Bruno "Bruno") was the first Elite Four member to appear in the anime (excluding Koga, who was later promoted to be one in [Generation II](https://lmts-personal.fandom.com/wiki/Generation_II "Generation II")), in _To Master the Onixpected_.
*   Lorelei appeared in _The Mandarin Island Miss Match_, but she is named "Prima" in the English dub.
*   Lance debuted in _Talkin' 'Bout an Evolution_, where he was mentioned to be the [Champion](https://lmts-personal.fandom.com/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Champion "Pokémon Champion") rather than a regular member of the Elite Four. He is referred to as a member of the Elite Four in _Flash of the Titans!_. From _Aim For The Eight!_ onwards, he's referred to as the Champion once again, with him being mentioned to have claimed that title recently.
*   Agatha appeared in _The Scheme Team_, where she was acting as a temporary [Gym Leader](https://lmts-personal.fandom.com/wiki/Gym_Leader "Gym Leader") for the Viridian Gym. 
    *   Koga, though not an Elite Four member, debuted in _The Ninja Poké-Showdown_, where he had a Gym battle against Ash.

#### Hoenn Elite Four[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Flmts-personal.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FElite_Four%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D17&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")]

In [Hoenn](https://lmts-personal.fandom.com/wiki/Hoenn "Hoenn"), Ash has met only one Elite Four member:

*   Drake appeared in _Vanity Affair_, where he invited Ash and his friends to his boat, where he had a battle with Ash. He reappeared in _Looking Out for Number Two!_, where he was shown to have become a treasure hunter in addition to his Elite Four duties.

[File:LGPE Elite Four (LGPE).png](https://lmts-personal.fandom.com/wiki/Special:Upload?wpDestFile=LGPE_Elite_Four_(LGPE).png "File:LGPE Elite Four (LGPE).png")

Artwork of Chase and Elaine confronting the Kanto Elite Four in [Pokémon: Let's Go, Pikachu! and Let's Go, Eevee!](https://lmts-personal.fandom.com/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon:_Let%27s_Go,_Pikachu!_and_Let%27s_Go,_Eevee! "Pokémon: Let's Go, Pikachu! and Let's Go, Eevee!")

The **Elite Four** (Japanese: **四天王**_The Big Four_) are four [Pokémon Trainers](https://lmts-personal.fandom.com/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Trainer "Pokémon Trainer") who are regarded as the toughest in their [regional](https://lmts-personal.fandom.com/wiki/Region "Region")[Pokémon League](https://lmts-personal.fandom.com/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_League "Pokémon League"), just short of the [Pokémon League Champion](https://lmts-personal.fandom.com/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Champion "Pokémon Champion"). Those who challenge the Elite Four must have won all eight [Badges](https://lmts-personal.fandom.com/wiki/Badge "Badge") from that region (or, for Trainers in [Alola](https://lmts-personal.fandom.com/wiki/Alola "Alola"), must have completed all of their island challenge trials). To become Champion, Trainers must face all four and the current Champion consecutively without losing to any of them. Challengers who lose at any time must start their challenge from the beginning. In Paldea, the challenge is named the Elite Test, and is part of the greater Champion Assessment.

One group resides at the Indigo Plateau in [Kanto](https://lmts-personal.fandom.com/wiki/Kanto "Kanto") and are considered the best Trainers in both Kanto and [Johto](https://lmts-personal.fandom.com/wiki/Johto "Johto"). Another group is located in Ever Grande City in [Hoenn](https://lmts-personal.fandom.com/wiki/Hoenn "Hoenn"), while another is located on Mount Lanakila in [Alola](https://lmts-personal.fandom.com/wiki/Alola "Alola"). Four more groups reside at the Pokémon Leagues in Sinnoh, Unova, Kalos, and Template:Pal.

In the games, they use strong medicine items in battles. In [Generation II](https://lmts-personal.fandom.com/wiki/Generation_II "Generation II"), they use Max Potions, and from [Generation III](https://lmts-personal.fandom.com/wiki/Generation_III "Generation III") onwards, they use Full Restores. Like [Gym Leaders](https://lmts-personal.fandom.com/wiki/Gym_Leader "Gym Leader"), they typically specialize in Pokémon of a particular [type](https://lmts-personal.fandom.com/wiki/Type "Type"). Prior to [Generation V](https://lmts-personal.fandom.com/wiki/Generation_V "Generation V") and in Generation IX, the Elite Four typically progresses in level with their Pokémon in the games and must be challenged in a set order. From Generation V to Generation VII, all members of the Elite Four (except in remakes) use Pokémon of the same levels, as they can be challenged in any order.

In [Generation VIII](https://lmts-personal.fandom.com/wiki/Generation_VIII "Generation VIII"), the Pokémon League in the Galar region uses the Champion Cup tournament instead of an Elite Four.

In the [Pokémon anime](https://lmts-personal.fandom.com/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_anime "Pokémon anime"), [Ash](https://lmts-personal.fandom.com/wiki/Ash_Ketchum "Ash Ketchum") and [his friends](https://lmts-personal.fandom.com/wiki/Ash%27s_friends "Ash's friends") infrequently meet Elite Four members, who then impart them with battle strategies. In _An Elite Meet and Greet!_, Lucian revealed that when a Trainer wins their respective region's [League Conference](https://lmts-personal.fandom.com/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_League_Conference "Pokémon League Conference"), they can participate in the [Champion League](https://lmts-personal.fandom.com/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_League#Champion_League "Pokémon League"), fighting the members of that region's Elite Four, and, if victorious against them, the regional [Champion](https://lmts-personal.fandom.com/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Champion "Pokémon Champion") as well. It has also been shown that an Elite Four member can challenge the Champion for their title.

The **Elite Four** (Japanese: **四天王**_The Big Four_[[1]](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Elite_Four#cite_note-1)) are four [Pokémon Trainers](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Trainer "Pokémon Trainer") who are regarded as the toughest in their [regional](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Region "Region")[Pokémon League](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_League "Pokémon League"), just short of the [Pokémon League Champion](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Champion "Pokémon Champion"). Those who challenge the Elite Four must have won all eight [Badges](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Badge "Badge") from that region (or, for Trainers in [Alola](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Alola "Alola"), must have completed all of their [island challenge](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Island_challenge "Island challenge") trials). To become Champion, Trainers must face all four and the current Champion consecutively without losing to any of them. Challengers who lose at any time must start their challenge from the beginning. In [Paldea](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Paldea "Paldea"), the challenge is named the Elite Test, and is part of the greater Champion Assessment.

One group resides at the [Indigo Plateau](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Indigo_Plateau "Indigo Plateau") in [Kanto](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Kanto "Kanto") and are considered the best Trainers in both Kanto and [Johto](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Johto "Johto"). Another group is located in [Ever Grande City](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Ever_Grande_City "Ever Grande City") in [Hoenn](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Hoenn "Hoenn"), while another is located on [Mount Lanakila](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Mount_Lanakila "Mount Lanakila") in [Alola](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Alola "Alola"). Four more groups reside at the Pokémon Leagues in [Sinnoh](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_League_(Sinnoh) "Pokémon League (Sinnoh)"), [Unova](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_League_(Unova) "Pokémon League (Unova)"), [Kalos](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_League_(Kalos) "Pokémon League (Kalos)"), and [Paldea](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_League_(Paldea) "Pokémon League (Paldea)").

In the games, they use strong [medicine](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Category:Medicine "Category:Medicine") items in battles. In [Generation II](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Generation_II "Generation II"), they use [Max Potions](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Max_Potion "Max Potion"), and from [Generation III](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Generation_III "Generation III") onwards, they use [Full Restores](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Full_Restore "Full Restore"). Like [Gym Leaders](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Gym_Leader "Gym Leader"), they typically specialize in Pokémon of a particular [type](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Type "Type"). Prior to [Generation V](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Generation_V "Generation V") and in [Paldea](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Paldea "Paldea"), the Elite Four typically progresses in [level](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Level "Level") with their Pokémon in the games and must be challenged in a set order. From Generation V to Generation VII, all members of the Elite Four (except in [remakes](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Remake "Remake")) use Pokémon of the same levels, as they can be challenged in any order. At [Blueberry Academy](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Blueberry_Academy "Blueberry Academy"), [Crispin](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Crispin "Crispin")'s Pokémon are one level lower than the others, but the Elite Four can be battled in any order.

The [Pokémon League](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Galar_League "Galar League") in the [Galar](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Galar "Galar") region is the only one to not have an Elite Four, instead using the Champion Cup tournament.

### Indigo Elite Four

At the [Indigo Plateau](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Indigo_Plateau "Indigo Plateau") — the site of the Pokémon League in [Kanto](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Kanto "Kanto") and [Johto](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Johto "Johto") — the Elite Four must be battled in a fixed order.

The **Elite Four** (Japanese: **四天王**_The Big Four_[[1]](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Elite_Four#cite_note-1)) are four [Pokémon Trainers](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Trainer "Pokémon Trainer") who are regarded as the toughest in their [regional](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Region "Region")[Pokémon League](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_League "Pokémon League"), just short of the [Pokémon League Champion](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Champion "Pokémon Champion"). Those who challenge the Elite Four must have won all eight [Badges](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Badge "Badge") from that region (or, for Trainers in [Alola](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Alola "Alola"), must have completed all of their [island challenge](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Island_challenge "Island challenge") trials). To become Champion, Trainers must face all four and the current Champion consecutively without losing to any of them. Challengers who lose at any time must start their challenge from the beginning. In [Paldea](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Paldea "Paldea"), the challenge is named the Elite Test, and is part of the greater Champion Assessment.

One group resides at the [Indigo Plateau](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Indigo_Plateau "Indigo Plateau") in [Kanto](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Kanto "Kanto") and are considered the best Trainers in both Kanto and [Johto](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Johto "Johto"). Another group is located in [Ever Grande City](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Ever_Grande_City "Ever Grande City") in [Hoenn](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Hoenn "Hoenn"), while another is located on [Mount Lanakila](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Mount_Lanakila "Mount Lanakila") in [Alola](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Alola "Alola"). Four more groups reside at the Pokémon Leagues in [Sinnoh](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_League_(Sinnoh) "Pokémon League (Sinnoh)"), [Unova](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_League_(Unova) "Pokémon League (Unova)"), [Kalos](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_League_(Kalos) "Pokémon League (Kalos)"), and [Paldea](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_League_(Paldea) "Pokémon League (Paldea)").

In the games, they use strong [medicine](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Category:Medicine "Category:Medicine") items in battles. In [Generation II](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Generation_II "Generation II"), they use [Max Potions](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Max_Potion "Max Potion"), and from [Generation III](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Generation_III "Generation III") onwards, they use [Full Restores](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Full_Restore "Full Restore"). Like [Gym Leaders](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Gym_Leader "Gym Leader"), they typically specialize in Pokémon of a particular [type](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Type "Type"). Prior to [Generation V](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Generation_V "Generation V") and in [Paldea](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Paldea "Paldea"), the Elite Four typically progresses in [level](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Level "Level") with their Pokémon in the games and must be challenged in a set order. From Generation V to Generation VII, all members of the Elite Four (except in [remakes](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Remake "Remake")) use Pokémon of the same levels, as they can be challenged in any order. At [Blueberry Academy](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Blueberry_Academy "Blueberry Academy"), [Crispin](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Crispin "Crispin")'s Pokémon are one level lower than the others, but the Elite Four can be battled in any order.

The [Pokémon League](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Galar_League "Galar League") in the [Galar](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Galar "Galar") region is the only one to not have an Elite Four, instead using the Champion Cup tournament.
